source_snapshot.procedure: Prepare an NFS share, locally mount the example export, use BMC WebUI/Remote Console to mount the image, and notes that the ISO can later be used to install an OS.
source_snapshot.criteria: Remote Console connects; the CD-ROM mounts and an Auto-install program appears.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; parameterized NFS path plus host block-device checks, with attended WebUI work.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED for mount-versus-install scope, NFS security, disk protection and cleanup.

old_problem: The old review treated a missing project export and an ambiguous sentence about possible OS installation as a permanent engineering decision. It also could not rely on the source's username/password wording as a valid generic NFS security contract.
disposition_reason: The title and acceptance text establish a reversible endpoint: Remote Console works, the approved NFS image is exposed as virtual optical media, and the auto-install landing screen is visible. The test stops there. NFS version/security and whether this BMC actually implements an NFS backend are project/OEM readiness inputs, not facts inferred from generic OpenBMC. No installer continuation or disk write is authorized or credited.
decision_basis: Exact XLSX row 745, its DeepSeek columns, GPT V2 object and historical record were directly read.
OpenBMC's public virtual-media design documents CIFS/HTTPS legacy remote media, not a universal NFS backend; NFS support therefore requires model-specific capability/SOP evidence.
RFC 8881 defines NFSv4.1 security flavors, including RPCSEC_GSS and optional AUTH_SYS/AUTH_NONE, so a generic username/password instruction is not an authoritative security model.
ED-35 preserves the unexecuted installation distinction, while ED-36 permits project bindings to remain readiness prerequisites rather than permanent BLOCKED.

test_case.test_name: Mount an approved NFS image through the supported BMC virtual-media path and verify installer visibility
test_case.purpose: Verify the project-qualified BMC NFS virtual-media feature presents the exact approved image as a virtual CD-ROM, Remote Console shows the expected installer/auto-install landing screen, and media is removed without modifying boot order or storage.
required_package: Model-specific evidence that this BMC/WebUI supports NFS virtual media and the approved operator SOP
Exact NFS server/export/image, immutable hash, NFS version and approved security flavor/export policy
Isolated SUT, baseline boot order and complete protected-disk inventory
Trusted read-only host device tools and an evidence destination outside virtual media
test_case.test_command: Operator confirms the WebUI exposes the project-approved NFS method, enters the approved server/export/image using the OEM SOP, and activates it in Remote Console. Agent may collect trusted pre/post `lsblk -o NAME,PATH,TYPE,SIZE,RO,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS,MODEL,SERIAL` evidence. Stop after exact-image virtual-CD enumeration and visible installer/launcher landing page; do not choose Install/Next. Deactivate/eject through WebUI and verify removal. The source's host-side example mount is optional reachability evidence only and must never substitute for BMC mounting.
test_case.expected_result: Remote Console remains usable; BMC reports the approved NFS image active; one matching read-only virtual optical device appears; the expected installer/auto-install landing screen is visible without execution; deactivation removes the device and leaves physical disks, mounts and boot state unchanged with no unexpected BMC/host errors.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires project proof of NFS capability, exact-image identity, correlated WebUI/console and host-device evidence, launcher visibility and complete cleanup. FAIL covers a supported/configured feature that cannot mount, wrong media, console/device mismatch, unexpected write/boot, or failed removal. If NFS is absent, only authoritative Project SPEC may mark N/A; otherwise execution is not ready. Do not claim OS-installation PASS.
safety_gate: No hard-coded `192.168.0.169:/home/opt`; bind the exact approved export and security flavor
Do not assume username/password authentication, expose secrets, change boot order, continue the installer, partition or write any disk
Use read-only export/media semantics where supported and preserve storage/boot baselines
Stop on unplanned boot/installer advance, media mismatch or loss of independent console recovery; no automatic retry
Deactivate virtual media and any separately approved diagnostic client mount after evidence collection
expected_evidence: BMC model/firmware, NFS capability/SOP and WebUI/Remote Console screenshots
Redacted NFS endpoint/version/security/export metadata plus exact image hash
Pre/mounted/ejected device and boot/mount inventories identifying the virtual CD-ROM
Visible installer landing page, cleanup state and BMC/host health logs
test_case.recovery: On unintended boot or installer progress, do not confirm a prompt. Preserve console/device evidence, deactivate the virtual media through the approved BMC path, restore only the pre-approved boot state, unmount any diagnostic NFS client view, and escalate before reboot or retry.

source_conflict.preserved_original_conflict: The Master still mixes a host example mount, BMC media operation, generic credentials and later OS-install wording.
source_conflict.resolution: Each statement now has a bounded role: local mount is optional reachability evidence, BMC mount is the functional action, launcher visibility is acceptance, and actual installation is excluded.

blocked.reason: Core action, endpoint and recovery are now defined; OEM NFS support, export/security and image values are readiness inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: BMC NFS capability/SOP, export, NFS security, image, isolated SUT and storage baseline.
